summary: Add a small set of plain Java POJOs modelling a warehouse, the stores within it, storage locations, products, and the stock held at each location. Field and method sets are a best-guess starting point, as the author requested.
approach: Create a new package com.neversoft.warehouse under src/main/java, following the conventions of the existing Vehicle POJO: public class, private fields, no-arg and all-args constructors, getters/setters, and equals/hashCode/toString. The repo has no build tool and package.json compiles with plain javac --release 25 -Xlint:all -Werror, so the classes stay dependency-free. Five classes: Warehouse (root; id, name, address, list of Stores), Store (named area within a warehouse; id, name, warehouseId, list of Locations), Location (physical slot such as aisle/rack/shelf/bin; id, code, storeId, optional capacity), Product (catalogue item; id, SKU, name, description, unit of measure) and StockItem (the relationship between a location and the stock in it; links a locationId to a Product with a quantity, and is the only place quantity lives, so a location can hold many products and a product can be stocked in many locations). Parent/child links go downward as lists (Warehouse to Store to Location); upward links are plain ids, as Vehicle uses a long id, which avoids object cycles that would break equals/hashCode/toString. A few small domain helpers are included (adding a child to a list, adjusting stock quantity without going negative). Following the repo pattern, a dependency-free test harness is added and the hardcoded package.json test script, which currently names only the Vehicle files, is extended to compile and run the warehouse sources and tests too.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The author asked for POJOs and the fields will change, so mutable classes matching Vehicle are more consistent.
They create cycles in equals/hashCode/toString and the author asked for simple POJOs; ids are enough.

alternatives_considered.option: Store quantity directly on Location or Product
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A location can hold many products and a product can sit in many locations, so a separate StockItem models the relationship properly.
Would add dependencies and a build system the repo does not have, and the author asked for plain POJOs.
Out of scope for the request.

components: Java domain model (new package com.neversoft.warehouse) - new Warehouse, Store, Location, Product and StockItem classes
Java tests (new package under src/test/java) - new dependency-free test harness covering the classes, in the style of VehicleTest
Root package.json test script - extended so npm test compiles and runs the warehouse sources and tests as well as the existing Vehicle ones
assumptions: "Stores" means sub-areas or sections within a warehouse, not retail stores.
"Locations" are physical storage positions, such as aisle/rack/shelf/bin, belonging to a store.
"Stock" means a quantity of a product at a location.
Target is Java 25, matching the existing --release 25 build script.
Plain long ids and int quantities are acceptable, as with Vehicle; there is no persistence, so no id generation is needed.
The request for methods is met by accessors plus a minimal set of domain helpers; no services, repositories or business logic are required.
Adding tests and extending the package.json test script is in scope, following the issue #1 convention.

risks.risk: Guessed fields and relationships do not match the author's intent
risks.mitigation: State the assumptions in the PR description; keep the classes simple and the design provisional, as the author invited.

risks.risk: Id-based upward links may be less convenient than object references
risks.mitigation: Easy to change later, and it avoids cycles in equals/hashCode/toString.

risks.risk: Extending the hardcoded npm test script could break the existing Vehicle test
risks.mitigation: Keep the Vehicle compile and run steps intact; verify that both the Vehicle and warehouse tests pass.

risks.risk: -Xlint:all -Werror turns lint warnings into build failures
risks.mitigation: Avoid raw types and unchecked code, and run npm test before finishing.

risks.risk: Mutable lists exposed through getters allow external modification
risks.mitigation: Accept for a POJO and be consistent with the plain POJO request; document it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Public classes Warehouse, Store, Location, Product and StockItem exist in package com.neversoft.warehouse under src/main/java/com/neversoft/warehouse/, with the package declaration matching the directory.
Each class is a plain POJO with private fields, a no-arg constructor, an all-args constructor, and a getter and setter for every field; there are no annotations or external dependencies.
Each class overrides equals, hashCode and toString consistently over its fields; these are null-safe and do not recurse infinitely.
A Warehouse holds a list of Stores and a Store holds a list of Locations; child lists are never null on a default-constructed object.
StockItem associates a location with a Product and a quantity; the model allows one location to hold several products and one product to be stocked in several locations.
Quantity changes on StockItem (add and remove) reject negative resulting quantities and invalid arguments, with a documented exception.
Tests for the new classes exist and pass via npm test, and the existing VehicleTest still passes.
All sources compile with javac --release 25 -Xlint:all -Werror with no warnings.
Apart from the package.json test script, no existing file is modified.
